A common cause: htmx requests only carry the CSRF token if it's in the request, and moving the form into a partial may have dropped the token from the form itself. Putting {% csrf_token %} inside the form in the partial, or sending the token via hx-headers on the body, fixes it. I haven't seen your templates, so that's the first thing to check.

They aren't the same. Keep-alive just reuses one TCP connection for requests one after another, so a slow response blocks the ones behind it, which is why browsers open several connections. HTTP/2 multiplexing interleaves many request and response streams on a single connection, though TCP-level head-of-line blocking still exists (HTTP/3 addresses it).

`using` declares a resource that is disposed automatically when the scope exits, even on throw: `using x = open()` calls x[Symbol.dispose]() at the end of the block. `await using` does the same with Symbol.asyncDispose, and multiple resources dispose in reverse order. You need TS 5.2+, and runtime support varies, so check the Node version or polyfill.
